prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Monthly mean ozone by monitoring station (language en).
Grid: 13 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Station" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 8: header "Jul" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Aug" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 10: header "Sep" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 11: header "Oct" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 12: header "Nov" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 13: header "Dec" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 725px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 724px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly mean ozone levels across six monitoring stations, revealing seasonal patterns and station-to-station differences.","reading":"Readers locate a station in column 1, scan horizontally across months within that row, and compare stations vertically within a given month. The month columns form one chronological analytical sequence; the station column is the row key.","groups":["Column 1 (Station): row identifier, should be visually distinct from the data field.","Columns 2–13 (Jan–Dec): one chronological sequence; can be read as quarters Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec."],"keep_intact":["Station names on one line","Month abbreviations on one line","All numeric values, including decimal points, on one line"],"may_wrap":["None; all cells are short and should remain single-line. Wrapping station names would weaken row identification and scanning."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [110, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51] · table 723×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [128, 48, 49, 49, 49, 49, 49, 49, 49, 49, 49, 49, 48] · table 715×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [86, 54, 54, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"Everything stays on one line, no header wraps, no mid-word splits; the month columns are perfectly uniform so the twelve months read as one even sequence, and the table nearly fills the 725px measure (723). The station column is clearly separated from the data field, so row identification is unambiguous.","problems":"The station column is over-generous while the numeric columns are starved: 'Riverside'/'Station' sit in 89px of text for a 65px word, leaving a conspicuous dead gutter after the names, yet each month gets only 30px for 28px of digits, so values like 24.1 sit about 1px from the cell rule. The result reads as 'wide label, squeezed numbers' — the eye is pulled to the empty space at the left instead of to the values being compared.","cause":"Col 1 was given 110px (≈24px surplus) and the 12 month columns only 51px (2px surplus each). Shifting ~20px from col 1 to the months would have given every number 3–4px of breathing room with no loss to the station label."},{"design":"r0B","good":"Very strong hierarchy: the station column unmistakably reads as the row key, months remain a uniform block, and all cells stay single-line.","problems":"This is the worst imbalance of the three. The station column is enormously padded (107px of text for a 65px word — 42px of surplus) while Jan and Dec get exactly 27px for 27px of content, i.e. zero slack; in the render '24.1' and '23.5' nearly touch the column rules and look cramped and clipped-in-waiting. The table is also only 715px wide, so 9px of the available measure is simply wasted.","cause":"Col 1 = 128px starves the edge months, which were set to 48px (= exact minimum 48). The 42px of col-1 surplus could have added ~3.5px to every month column and still left the station name comfortable."},{"design":"r0C","good":"The best proportion of the three: months are the widest columns at 53–54px, so each value gets 32–33px of text and a comfortable 2–2.5px gap on both sides; the numeric field is calm and easy to scan vertically, and the table fills the measure exactly (725).","problems":"The station column is now the tightest thing on the page: 86px means exactly 65px of text for a 65px word, so 'Station' and 'Riverside' sit flush against the column divider while the numbers float in generous space. That inverts the intended hierarchy — the row key should be the most relaxed element, not the most constrained. There is also a pointless 1px irregularity (Apr = 53 vs 54 for the rest) that neither reads as a group nor helps any value.","cause":"Col 1 was set to its absolute minimum 86px; the surplus that would have given the labels 3–4px of slack was spent on month columns that already had enough."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"balanced-slack","widths":[90,52,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,53,52],"change":"Sets a single rule: every column gets ~4px of internal slack on each side. Station drops from 110/128 to 90 (69px of text for the 65px longest word — just enough to stop it touching the rule), Jan and Dec get 52 because their content is 1px narrower, and the ten 28px months get 53. This fixes both r0A's dead left gutter and r0B's zero-slack edge months, and gives the numbers the same breathing room as the labels instead of less."},{"name":"station-lead","widths":[100,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52,52],"change":"Keeps a deliberate hierarchy — the station column stays visibly the widest at 100px (79px of text, 14px of slack) so the row key anchors the left edge — but holds all twelve months at an identical 52px so the chronological sequence is perfectly even and each value gets 31px for 28px of digits. This is the r0A idea corrected: the label keeps its lead without stealing the numbers' margin, and the widths sum exactly to 724."},{"name":"quarter-cue","widths":[91,52,52,52,55,52,52,55,52,52,55,52,52],"change":"New idea: use width itself to hint the quarter structure the reading notes call out. All months sit at 52px (31px of text) except Apr, Jul and Oct, which get 55px — a 3px extra gutter at each quarter boundary that groups Jan–Mar / Apr–Jun / Jul–Sep / Oct–Dec without adding any line or rule. Station is 91px so the labels keep a hair of slack rather than the exact-minimum 86 of r0C. If the quarter cue reads as noise, fall back to 'station-lead'."}]}
